note: Hard tasks whose exact answers live in the reference docs but where baseline Claude tends to approximate or err. Assertions check precise values.

evals.prompt: On the C64 SID 6581, using the standard envelope rate table: what is the exact ATTACK time for attack-rate value 11 ($B), and what is the DECAY/RELEASE time for decay-rate value 11? Also, what is the attack time for value 0 and the decay/release time for value 0?
assertions: Attack time for value 11 is 800 ms
Decay/Release time for value 11 is 2.4 seconds
Attack time for value 0 is 2 ms
Decay/Release time for value 0 is 6 ms

evals.prompt: On the C64 SID, what happens if I select the noise waveform at the same time as another waveform (e.g. noise + pulse) in a voice's control register, and how do I recover from it?
assertions: States the noise generator can lock up / go silent (the waveform output can freeze near zero)
States it stays silent until reset
Says it is reset by the TEST bit (or by RES / chip reset)

evals.prompt: Give the exact timing of the VIC-II: how many clock cycles per raster line and how many raster lines per frame for the PAL 6569, and for the NTSC 6567R8?
assertions: PAL 6569: 63 cycles per raster line
PAL 6569: 312 raster lines per frame
NTSC 6567R8: 65 cycles per raster line
NTSC 6567R8: 263 raster lines per frame

evals.prompt: State the exact Bad Line condition on the VIC-II — the precise relationship between the current raster line, the DEN bit, and the YSCROLL bits that triggers a bad line.
assertions: Raster line is in the range $30 to $F7 (48 to 247)
The low 3 bits of the raster line equal YSCROLL (RASTER & 7 == YSCROLL, the low 3 bits of $D011)
The DEN (display enable) bit was set at some point in raster line $30
Describes that on a bad line the VIC stalls the CPU to do the c-accesses (badline steals cycles)

evals.prompt: Give the exact SCREEN codes (the values you POKE into screen RAM at $0400, NOT the PETSCII/CHR$ codes) for these characters: the @ sign, the letter A, a space, and a reverse (inverted) space.
assertions: Screen code for @ is 0
Screen code for A is 1
Screen code for space is 32
Screen code for a reverse space is 160 (the normal code + 128)

evals.prompt: Give the exact PETSCII CHR$ codes for: switching to lower-case character set, cursor down, reverse-on (RVS ON), and the color white.
assertions: CHR$(14) switches to lower-case / text mode
CHR$(17) is cursor down
CHR$(18) is RVS ON (reverse on)
CHR$(5) is white

evals.prompt: On the 6526 CIA, explain precisely how WRITING to the interrupt control register (ICR, e.g. $DC0D) differs from READING it: what does bit 7 do on a write, and what happens to the interrupt flags when you read it?
assertions: On WRITE, bit 7 is the set/clear control: if bit 7 = 1 the 1-bits set (enable) those mask bits; if bit 7 = 0 the 1-bits clear (disable) them
On READ, the register returns the current interrupt flags
Reading the ICR CLEARS the interrupt flags (and acknowledges/de-asserts the interrupt)
Bit 7 on READ indicates whether an interrupt occurred (IR flag)

evals.prompt: Exactly how do I read the two paddles on the C64? Which CIA1 register/bits select which pair of paddles is connected to the SID, which SID registers return the paddle positions, and why is reading paddles awkward alongside the keyboard?
assertions: The paddle position values are read from SID registers $D419 (POTX) and $D41A (POTY)
CIA1 port A ($DC00) bits 6 and 7 select which control port's paddle pair is routed to the SID
Notes the keyboard matrix shares CIA1 port A, so keyboard scanning interferes with paddle selection (must disable/avoid keyscan)
Each port has two paddles (X and Y), giving four total across the two ports

evals.prompt: On the C64, describe exactly the memory configuration the CPU sees for these values of the $01 processor port: $37 (default), $35, and $34. For each, state what occupies $A000-$BFFF, $D000-$DFFF, and $E000-$FFFF.
assertions: $37: BASIC ROM at $A000-$BFFF, I/O at $D000-$DFFF, KERNAL ROM at $E000-$FFFF
$35: RAM at $A000-$BFFF, I/O at $D000-$DFFF, RAM at $E000-$FFFF (BASIC and KERNAL ROM banked out, I/O still visible)
$34: RAM everywhere including $A000-$BFFF, $D000-$DFFF and $E000-$FFFF (I/O banked out, all RAM)
Correctly ties this to the LORAM/HIRAM/CHAREN bits (bits 0/1/2 of $01)

evals.prompt: When a BASIC SYS call transfers to machine code, exactly which memory addresses hold the A, X, Y register values and the processor status that are loaded into the CPU on entry (and stored back on RTS)?
assertions: Accumulator A is at $030C (780)
X register is at $030D (781)
Y register is at $030E (782)
Status register (SR/flags) is at $030F (783)

evals.prompt: Explain the exact bit layout of the VIC-II memory-pointer register $D018 (53272): which bits select the screen (video matrix) base and which select the character generator / bitmap base, and what address granularity each uses within the 16K VIC bank.
assertions: Bits 7-4 select the video matrix (screen RAM) base, in units of $0400 (1K) within the VIC bank
Bits 3-1 select the character generator base, in units of $0800 (2K) within the bank
In bitmap mode, bit 3 selects the bitmap base at $0000 or $2000 within the bank (8K granularity)
Bit 0 is unused

evals.prompt: Give the exact register-level calling contract for two KERNAL routines: SETLFS and GETIN. Which registers hold which inputs, and what is returned?
assertions: SETLFS: A = logical file number, X = device number, Y = secondary address
SETLFS is at $FFBA
GETIN: returns the input character in the accumulator A (0 if no key/character is available)
GETIN is at $FFE4

evals.prompt: What exactly does the original C64 power supply (the 'brick') output, and what is the well-known failure mode that damages the computer?
assertions: Supplies +5V DC (regulated)
Supplies 9V AC (unregulated)
The classic failure is the 5V regulator failing such that the 5V rail rises (overvoltage)
The overvoltage damages chips (RAM and/or other ICs)

evals.prompt: On a 1541, after I send a DOS command on the command channel, how do I read the error/status channel in BASIC, and what does the channel return after a command that succeeded? Give the exact response.
assertions: Open the command channel with OPEN 15,8,15 and read it with INPUT#15 (into four variables: code, message, track, sector)
A successful command returns error code 00
The success message text is OK
The track and sector fields are 00,00 on success
